method: Written by Claude Opus 5.5 from the Tamil verses alone, before any translation of these verses was read in this session. The model may still remember well-known verses, so this is not a pure test of reading.

kural:31.reading: Virtue yields distinction and wealth alike; what gain for a living being exceeds virtue?

kural:32.reading: There is no gain beyond virtue and no ruin beyond forgetting it.

kural:33.reading: In whatever way you are able, without ceasing, do virtuous deeds wherever they can be done.

kural:34.reading: Being stainless in mind is the whole of virtue; everything else is mere noise and show.

kural:35.reading: Virtue is what is carried out avoiding four things: envy, craving, anger and harsh words.

kural:36.reading: Do not say you will attend to it later; do virtue now, for it is the undying companion when you die.

kural:37.reading: No need to ask what virtue's way is: compare the palanquin's bearer and its rider. The likely traditional sense is that the rider shows virtue's fruit, but the verse could also warn against that inference.

kural:38.reading: If one does good without letting a day pass idle, that good is a stone blocking the road of one's further births.

kural:39.reading: Only what comes from virtue is true joy; everything else lies outside it and brings no praise.

kural:40.reading: What one ought to do is virtue; what one ought to escape is blame.

kural:371.reading: A fate of gain brings tireless effort; a fate of loss brings sloth.

kural:372.reading: A fate of loss makes a person foolish; a fate of gain, when it comes, broadens understanding.

kural:373.reading: Though one studies many subtle books, one's own innate understanding prevails over them.

kural:374.reading: The world has two distinct natures: wealth is one thing, and being wise is another.

kural:375.reading: In acquiring wealth, under fate, all that is good can turn out bad and all that is bad can turn out good.

kural:376.reading: What is not yours will not stay however you guard it; what is yours will not leave though you cast it away.

kural:377.reading: Except as the one who apportions has apportioned, even those who amass crores cannot enjoy it.

kural:378.reading: The destitute would renounce, if only what they are destined to suffer would pass without being inflicted on them.

kural:379.reading: Those who see things as good when good comes: why do they grieve when it does not?

kural:380.reading: What is stronger than fate? Even if one devises another way, it arrives first.

kural:392.reading: What are called numbers and what are called letters: these two are the eyes of living people.

kural:393.reading: Only the learned are said to have eyes; the unlearned have two sores on their faces.

kural:394.reading: Meeting with delight and parting so as to be thought of afterward: such is the scholar's way.

kural:395.reading: The learned yearn humbly, as the poor do before the rich; those who do not learn are the truly low.

kural:396.reading: A sand well yields water as far as it is dug; a person's knowledge flows as far as they have learned.

kural:397.reading: Since every land and town becomes one's own through learning, why does anyone stay unlearned until death?

kural:398.reading: Learning gained in a single birth protects a person through seven births.

kural:399.reading: Seeing the world delight in what delights them, the learned long for it all the more.

kural:400.reading: Learning is imperishable, excellent wealth; nothing else is truly wealth.

kural:971.reading: A person's radiance is abundance of spirit or resolve; disgrace is saying one will live without it.

kural:974.reading: Like the chastity of faithful women, greatness exists only when one holds oneself to it.

kural:975.reading: The truly great accomplish, by proper means, deeds that are hard to do.

kural:976.reading: The small-minded do not hold the aim of honouring and following the great.

kural:977.reading: When distinction falls to the unworthy, it issues in acts of excess.

kural:978.reading: Greatness always bows humbly; smallness adorns itself in self-admiration.

kural:979.reading: Greatness is freedom from arrogance; smallness is riding high on arrogance.

kural:980.reading: Greatness conceals others' failings; smallness speaks of nothing but faults.

kural:1093.reading: The lover speaks: she glanced, then looked down, and that was water poured on the love planted between us.

kural:1094.reading: The lover speaks: when I look, she looks at the ground; when I do not, she looks at me and smiles softly.

kural:1095.reading: The lover speaks: she does not look at me directly, but smiles as if narrowing one eye.

kural:1096.reading: Though they speak like strangers, the words of those who are not hostile are quickly understood.

kural:1097.reading: Small words without anger and looks like an enemy's are the signs of those who pretend to be strangers but are intimate.

kural:1098.reading: When I look, she softens and gently smiles; there is a particular beauty in this graceful one.

kural:1099.reading: Glancing in a general way, as strangers do, is found among lovers themselves.

kural:1100.reading: When eye meets eye in agreement, the words of the mouth serve no purpose.

naladiyar:131.reading: A fine topknot, a curved-border garment and turmeric are not true beauty; the beauty of learning, from a heart's balance that knows its own good, is true beauty.

naladiyar:132.reading: It benefits in this life, does not lessen by giving, illuminates oneself, and does not perish even when its holders are gone; in no world do we see a medicine like learning for curing confusion.

naladiyar:133.reading: The wise prize salt from barren land above paddy from fertile land; so the learned, even from the lowest place, are placed at the head.

naladiyar:134.reading: It cannot be taken from where it is stored, is not lost, and even angry kings cannot seize it; the legacy one should leave one's children is learning and nothing else.

naladiyar:135.reading: Learning has no shore, the learner's days are few, and illnesses many; so choose clearly what is fitting, like the bird that takes the milk and leaves the water.

naladiyar:136.reading: No one scorns a boatman as lowest of the old castes, for with his help one crosses the river; likewise take good things with the help of a learned person, whatever their birth.

naladiyar:137.reading: Only if it were sweeter than gathering and laughing with those of enduring learning, free of enmity and sharp of mind, would we look to the city of those who dwell in heaven.

naladiyar:138.reading: Lord of the cool shore: friendship with the learned is like eating sugarcane from the tip, growing sweeter; ties with the unkind are like eating it from the thick end, growing worse.

naladiyar:139.reading: Even the unlearned, by keeping company with the learned, gain sound knowledge day by day, as a new pot gives water fragrance from the pathiri flower.

naladiyar:140.reading: Without studying the books of knowledge, reciting worldly books is mere noisy chatter; such readers do not know how to end their confusion.
